did: I looked at whether we are rebuilding a video editor. Most of what we own is generic editor machinery, but no open tool keeps our rules together: the same bytes twice, offline on home, and a schema code checks. I tested OpenTimelineIO, MoviePy and melt here. The real risk for next week's scene tags is a third note model of our own, since Studio already pins notes to a scene and episode feedback pins them to a moment. It is all in issue 3003. Since then you set aside the generic scene tags, so I brought issue 3003 up to date with that.

calls.title: Scene tags build on the notes we already pin to a scene
options: Join Studio's scene notes and episode feedback
A new store for scene tags
calls.why: Studio's notes already follow a scene into later revisions, and the step cache already re-renders only changed scenes
calls.undo: Store tags elsewhere in a later story; the notes stay as written

calls.title: OpenTimelineIO is an export at most, never the cut list
options: Replace the cut list with it
calls.why: It holds our facts as opaque extras and has no maintained TypeScript or Rust library
calls.undo: Write the export when you want to open a render in a desktop editor

calls.title: Review stays on the phone, with no studio review server
options: Keep review in Studio on the phone
calls.why: You are the one reviewer, on Android
calls.undo: Stand up Kitsu later, after a licence call on AGPL

left: Cross-machine byte equality of MoviePy and melt was not tested, only the same machine twice
